Subject: Deployment mode confirmation + migration carve-outs

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying asks so we can build a concrete mutual action plan.

Recap (from our side)
- Primary constraint: PII + PCI-adjacent data; FinGate needs isolation and auditability.
- Options discussed: Redwood Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs), Private VPC / on-prem (full control).
- Current stack: mixture of self-hosted GPU nodes (K8s) + some calls to an external LLM API for non-PII features.

Asks / confirmation needed
1) Is the requirement "no external LLM API processing of PII" a hard security requirement or negotiable with strict egress controls?
2) Expected production steady-state throughput (tokens/sec or requests/sec) and peak concurrency so we can size Dedicated vs Private nodes.
3) Any procurement constraints on contract term (monthly vs 12/24mo commit)?

Proposed next steps
- We’ll draft two migration paths and a phased canary plan (big-bang is possible but higher risk).
- I’ve attached a short brief comparing a self-hosted migration vs Redwood Dedicated/Private (MAG-Redwood-vs-self-host-brief.pdf).
- Can we lock a 30–45 minute follow-up this week to confirm throughput and the procurement point?

If you prefer an initial technical-only session with your infra lead, we can loop them in — cc’ing Aditya to help coordinate.

Thanks,
— Soojin

Hi Soojin — thanks for the recap and the brief; useful. A few answers below.

1) Data handling: We cannot send PII to any external multi-tenant inference service. We can consider an external hosted API only if (a) it runs inside a dedicated tenancy managed for us, or (b) only non-PII traffic is routed to it. So effectively we need Dedicated or Private for PII flows.

2) Throughput: Steady-state ~40 requests/sec (average prompt ~600 tokens); expect spikes up to ~220 requests/sec during batch reconciliation windows. Concurrency target ~200 live requests.

3) Procurement: FinGate prefers a 12–24 month commit but needs T&C review. Procurement contact is procurement@fingate.com — they will send standard SOW terms.

Also — current infra: our internal K8s GPU pool runs mixed models (some fine-tuned). We are evaluating migrating inference off the cluster. The key questions for us are: downtime constraints (we prefer phased dual-run) and incremental cost profile for dedicated vs private VPC.

Can you include a short canary timeline and the sort of audit traces (logs/KV cache visibility, token accounting) we’d get? Also we need to confirm SOC2 evidence and a data retention SLA before we go to procurement.

Thanks — Alex

--
Alex Chen
Head of AI Platform, FinGate Inc.
alex.chen@fingate.com

Subject: Re: Deployment mode confirmation + migration carve-outs

Alex — perfect, that helps a lot. Below I outlined two pragmatic migration tracks and the canary/validation plan you asked for.

High-level recommendation
- For PII routes: Private VPC (customer-managed control plane or on-prem) if FinGate requires full network isolation + KMS/HSM integration. Dedicated capacity (reserved) is a close second if isolation can be achieved via a dedicated tenancy and strict egress controls.
- For non-PII features: Redwood Hosted API is the fastest path to offload costs.

Migration tracks
A) Phased dual-run (recommended)
  - Step 0: Mirror traffic to Redwood (traffic copy) for 2–4 weeks. No user-visible change.
  - Step 1: Canary routing: route 5–10% of production traffic to Redwood for 48–72 hours, validate outputs and latency SLOs.
  - Step 2: Gradual ramp (10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) over 2–4 weeks with automated rollback triggers (accuracy regression, latency > 2x baseline, error rate > 2%).
  - Validation: sample-based quality checks, end-to-end functional tests, and token/accounting reconciliation.

B) Big-bang cutover (only if timing/ops demands it)
  - Parallel run for 48hrs, then switch during a low-traffic window with pre-agreed rollback plan. Higher operational risk.

Canary timeline & observability
- Mirror: 2–4 weeks
- Canary: 48–72 hours per stage
- Metrics available: per-request latency histogram, token accounting at route level, KV cache hit rates, per-session trace IDs (trace IDs correlate to your logs), and model-version-level performance.
- Audit artifacts: request/response logs (redacted per PII policy), signed delivery receipts for retention events, and rollout audit trail.

SOC2 / evidence
- We can provide the SOC2 summary report and the SOC2 evidence bundle scoped for customers on Private or Dedicated plans. I’ve listed SOC2-evidence-summary.zip in attachments — we can redact any vendor-sensitive items before sharing with procurement.

Ballpark economics (initial guidance)
- Dedicated reserved pool: predictable monthly commit; lower per-token cost than Hosted for sustained high throughput.
- Private VPC/on-prem: higher up-front setup and infra fees; better for strict compliance and control.
- I’ll have Aditya add a short price sketch for 12/24mo commit options.

Next steps
- Aditya will follow up with a pricing sketch and outline SOW items.
- I’ll prepare a short mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and test criteria (attaching MAP-FinGate-mutual-action-plan.xlsx).
- Can we set follow-up Thursday 10:00 PT for a technical dive with your infra lead?

Cheers,
— Soojin

--

Alex / procurement team — looping in pricing and legal next steps.

Short pricing notes (ballpark, subject to final SOW):
- Dedicated reserved pool (12mo): estimated $18k–$28k / month depending on GPU class and commit size to meet ~200 concurrent requests and peak window. Includes network isolation options and standard SLAs.
- Private VPC (VPC deployment with KMS): setup fee one-time (typ. $60k–120k) + ongoing infra fee similar to Dedicated but with added service and compliance premium.

We’ll prepare a redlineable SOW and a short SLR (service level runbook) for the canary stages. Legal: laura_bennett@redwood.com is owning the SOW intake. Procurement, please share your standard SOW template and any mandatory clauses you require.

Credit note: We can offer an early-commitment onboarding credit (one month) for a 12mo reserved deal; details to be included in the SOW.

Thanks — Aditya

1) Please include a short appendix in the MAP that states the data retention SLA (we’re targeting 90 days +/- administrative hold options).
2) Confirm SOC2 summary and provide the assertion timeframe (we need a signed SOC2 Type II within the last 12 months for vendor assessment).

Procurement will share the SOW template this afternoon. Let’s keep the Thursday 10:00 PT technical dive — I’ll bring our infra lead (Ravi) and a product manager to validate regression criteria.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
